text: Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com A 4" countertop is now offered only while a Sink Base stands under the basin. If a lifted countertop carries the basin off its Sink Base, 4" disappears from Resize → Thickness and from the Countertop step, and it comes back once the basin is over a Sink Base again.Tested on: Urban Low Height, Urban Duplex (Custom and Prebuilt flows)Steps:1. Click the countertop → Resize → Thickness → 0.5", 4" and 5.1" are listed2. Pick 5.1" → click the countertop → Position → Drag & Drop → drag the countertop up, higher than 8" above the cabinets, so it takes the basin with it → Apply3. Click the countertop → Resize → Thickness → only 0.5" and 5.1" are listed4. Go to the Countertop step → Thickness shows only 0.5" and 5.1", and 5.1" is still selected5. Click the countertop → Position → Standard → the basin is back on the Sink Base, and 4" is listed again in the menu and on the Countertop stepExpected: 4" is offered only when the basin sits over a Sink Base. A lifted countertop that carries the basin offers 0.5" and 5.1".Video: https://monosnap.ai/file/AoqlFZMydFYFjR5GSpR3EZhEVoAOIRPlease check on your side and resolve if it works for you - or share the exact steps if something's still off.

author: oleh frolov
text: Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com When a thick countertop is moved so its basin is no longer over the Sink Base, that Sink Base now always turns into the matching Side Cabinet (same size, handle and colours). Before, if the countertop was set down again beside the row in the same drag, the cabinet could stay a Sink Base without its basin. Moving the countertop back makes it a Sink Base again.Tested on: Urban Low Height, Urban DuplexSteps:1. Countertop step → Thickness 5.1" → click the countertop → Position → Drag & Drop2. Lift the countertop and move it so the basin is no longer over the Sink Base → Apply → the cabinet that held the basin is now a Side Cabinet3. Repeat, but set the countertop down again beside the row in the same drag → Apply → the same: the Sink Base becomes a Side Cabinet4. Click the countertop → Position → Standard → the basin lands back and the cabinet is a Sink Base again5. Open the Summary after step 2 → the cabinet is listed as a Side Cabinet, not a Sink BaseExpected: as soon as the basin leaves its Sink Base, that cabinet becomes a Side Cabinet; if the change can't be completed, the countertop goes back with the message "The sink could not move with the countertop, so the countertop went back."Video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aKEf0Zcnf3GowsKhrbxZXwPDJRH84w8g/view?usp=sharingPlease check on your side and resolve if it works for you - or share the exact steps if something's still off.

author: oleh frolov
text: Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com A Sink Base added with Drag to Place could land without its basin, so it looked like a Side Cabinet. It now comes in as a Sink Base with its basin and the countertop's thickness - the same as a cabinet added with "+". Also, on an empty scene the first cabinet added with Drag to Place now goes in right away, with its countertop.Tested on: Urban Low Height, Urban DuplexSteps:1. Prebuilt → Urban Low Height → switch to Custom2. Cabinet Type: Sink Base → Cabinet Style: 1 Drawer → Drag to Place3. Drag the new cabinet next to the upper Sink Base → Apply → a Sink Base with its basin is added under the same countertop4. Start an empty Cabinet Builder → Side Cabinet → 1 Drawer → Drag to Place → the cabinet goes in right away, with its countertop5. Sink Base → 1 Drawer → Drag to Place → drag it next to the first cabinet → Apply → the Sink Base stands next to it with its basin, and the countertop covers bothExpected: Drag to Place adds exactly the cabinet you picked in the builder, with its basin and countertop, the same as "+".Video: https://monosnap.ai/file/leDr9HfYc4jXBST4NFYslqEfYUBw7FPlease check on your side and let me know if it works for you - or share the exact steps if something's still off.

author: oleh frolov
text: Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com In the countertop's menu, "Thickness" is now "Resize" with two options: Thickness and Length. Length shows only for a thick countertop (4", 5 1/8" or 5 1/2") and opens the countertop with handles on both ends, so you can drag an end to change its length.Tested on: Urban Low Height, Urban Duplex (Custom and Prebuilt flows)Steps:1. Countertop step → Thickness 0.5" → click the countertop → Resize → only Thickness is listed2. Thickness 4" (or 5.1") → click the countertop → Resize → Thickness and Length are listed3. Resize → Length → handles appear on both ends of the countertop4. Drag the right end → the length follows (e.g. 23.6" → 27.8") → Apply → the new length stays5. Resize → Thickness: in Custom it lists the thicknesses to pick from; in Prebuilt it opens the Thickness section of the Countertop stepExpected: there is no "Thickness" item on the menu's first level; Resize holds Thickness and, for a 4" / 5 1/8" / 5 1/2" countertop, Length with handles on both ends.Video: https://monosnap.ai/file/Uyr5dDPWqf9dki9vfbOCtg1AKN8T3KPlease check on your side and resolve if it works for you - or share the exact steps if something's still off.

author: Andriy Lobatskiy
text: Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com, this one is fixed and ready for review.What we fixedThe countertop can now be lengthened or shortened with the end handles while it stays on the cabinets, and the basin stays centered on the SB cabinet. We also smoothed the countertop drag and the snapping of the top and basin near cabinet edges. How we tested1. Built a run of an SB cabinet with another cabinet next to it, 4" countertop.2. Selected the countertop and dragged each end handle to lengthen and shorten it.3. Tried to shorten it past the SB cabinet from both ends.4. Switched to 5-⅛" and 5-½" tops and repeated steps 2–3, then moved the top around and close to the cabinet edges.5. Checked that handles don't appear for other thicknesses.Expected result- Only the dragged end moves; the opposite end and the basin (centered on the SB) stay in place.- The top can't become shorter than the SB cabinet and always fully covers it — with the SB on the right, only the left end can be shortened. - Handles are available only on 4", 5-⅛" and 5-½" tops.- Movement mode depends on thickness: 4" = Offset (stays at cabinet height, slides left/right along the cabinets); 5-⅛" and 5-½" = Remote (moves freely left/right and up/down, also off the cabinets).- Dragging is smooth, and near cabinet edges the top and the basin settle onto the edge without a jump.
